installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# MultiForge Installation Script
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server

apt update -y
apt install -y curl jq unzip file

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server || exit 1

## Resolve the download URL for the fork installer jar
if [ "${MULTIFORGE_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
    echo "-- Resolving latest MultiForge release via the GitHub API --"
    RESOLVED_URL=$(curl -sSL https://api.github.com/repos/0xnullsect0r/MultiForge/releases/latest \
        | jq -r '.assets[] | select(.name | test("^multiforge-.*-installer\\.jar$")) | .browser_download_url')

    if [ -z "${RESOLVED_URL}" ] || [ "${RESOLVED_URL}" = "null" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: could not resolve a multiforge-*-installer.jar asset from the latest GitHub release."
        exit 1
    fi
else
    RESOLVED_URL=$(echo "${DOWNLOAD_URL}" | sed "s/{VERSION}/${MULTIFORGE_VERSION}/g")
fi

echo "-- Resolved download URL: ${RESOLVED_URL} --"

## Download the fork installer jar
curl -sSL -o multiforge-installer.jar "${RESOLVED_URL}"

## Sanity check the downloaded file before trusting it
FILE_TYPE=$(file -b multiforge-installer.jar)
case "${FILE_TYPE}" in
    *Zip*|*Java*|*archive*)
        echo "-- Downloaded file looks like a valid archive (${FILE_TYPE}) --"
        ;;
    *)
        echo "ERROR: downloaded file does not look like a jar/zip archive."
        echo "-- file(1) reports: ${FILE_TYPE} --"
        echo "-- First 200 bytes of the file: --"
        head -c 200 multiforge-installer.jar
        echo ""
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

## Run the MultiForge fork installer against /mnt/server
echo "-- Running MultiForge installer (targeting Minecraft ${MC_VERSION}) --"
java -jar multiforge-installer.jar --installServer /mnt/server
INSTALL_EXIT=$?

if [ ${INSTALL_EXIT} -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: multiforge-installer.jar exited with code ${INSTALL_EXIT}"
    exit ${INSTALL_EXIT}
fi

## Clean up installer artifacts we no longer need
rm -f multiforge-installer.jar
rm -f ./*.log

## The installer lays down libraries/net/neoforged/neoforge/<v>/unix_args.txt.
## The startup command expects unix_args.txt at the server root, so symlink it.
ARGS_PATH=$(find libraries -name 'unix_args.txt' 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
if [ -n "${ARGS_PATH}" ]; then
    echo "-- Linking ${ARGS_PATH} -> unix_args.txt --"
    ln -sf "${ARGS_PATH}" unix_args.txt
else
    echo "WARNING: could not locate a libraries/**/unix_args.txt after install."
fi

## Fetch a default server.properties if the installer did not provide one
if [ ! -f server.properties ]; then
    echo "-- Fetching a default server.properties --"
    curl -sSL -o server.properties https://raw.githubusercontent.com/parkervcp/eggs/master/game_eggs/minecraft/java/forge/server.properties
fi

## Accept the EULA
echo "eula=true" > eula.txt

## Ensure the standard mod/config directories exist.
## NOTE: we intentionally do NOT seed config/multiforge-server.toml here -
## the MultiForge installer writes its own on first boot. Overwriting it
## here would clobber installer-provided defaults.
mkdir -p mods
mkdir -p config

echo "MultiForge installation complete."
